Islam guarantees the right of the accused to present evidence and defend themselves (*"لَا يَقْضِ الْقَاضِي بَيْنَ النَّاسِ عَلَى جَهْلٍ"* – *"The judge should not rule based on ignorance"*). - If the judge denies the accused a fair chance to prove innocence, this violates Islamic principles of justice. 4. **Hastiness and Prejudice (Al-Istihlal wa Al-Ihtikar)**: - It violates the principle of **presumption of innocence**. - It denies the accused their **right to defend themselves**. - It shows **hastiness and potential bias**, which are forbidden in Islamic justice. - It could lead to **oppression (zulm)**, which is strongly condemned in Islam. ### **What Should Have Happened?** - The judge should have **allowed the accused to present evidence**. - The case should have been **thoroughly investigated** before a verdict. -
